decisions.statement: Whether a node can be asked for its parent is named rather than passed as a bare flag.
A line is answered counting from the first line.
The text a literal node carries is answered without the quotes around it.
A caller asking for every piece of a template literal is answered each of them.
A node is answered at where its own text starts past whatever trivia leads the node.
The object literal a declaration has is answered past whatever casts wrap the object literal.
Whether a declaration is exported is read from the modifiers that declaration has.
Whether a node scopes the names declared inside it is answered here.
An import naming nothing at all carries more than types.
An import of an empty list of names reads as types alone and as not erased.
A fault the parse recovered from is answered rather than dropped.
A body the parser had no fault with is answered as having none.
The fault answered is the first one, read as one line of text.
Nothing here judges a body or knows why the body is read.
A path is a name the parse has so a node says its place rather than a file this module opens.

definition: a body read as TypeScript, and where in that reading a thing is
